introduction: Christ is risen, alleluia! On this Easter Sunday the whole Church rejoices. Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and runs to tell Peter and the beloved disciple, who see and believe. Peter, who once denied the Lord, now stands up as a witness to his Resurrection. Paul invites us to seek the things that are above, where Christ is. Today we renew the promises of our Baptism. Let us celebrate with joy the day the Lord has made.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ is risen and has given us new life. Full of Easter joy, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a joyful witness to the Resurrection in every place and every language. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the newly baptized of this Easter: that they may grow in faith, supported by the love of their communities. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who mourn, who are sick, or who feel that hope has died: that the risen Christ may meet them and give them new life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in the world: that the Lord who conquered death may break the power of violence and hatred. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves and our families: that we may carry the joy of Easter into our homes and set our hearts on the things that are above. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, by raising your Son from the dead you have opened for us the way to eternal life. May the joy of this day remain in us and in all who believe. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: He saw and believed
reflection.body:
The first Easter morning begins in the dark. Mary Magdalene goes to the tomb "while it was still dark" and finds the stone taken away. Her first thought is not resurrection but theft: "They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don't know where they have laid him!"

Peter and the other disciple run to the tomb. John remembers the details: "They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first." He waits, Peter goes in, and they see the linen cloths lying there and the head cloth rolled up by itself. Then the other disciple enters, "and he saw and believed." John adds an honest note: "For as yet they didn't know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead." Faith comes before full understanding.

In the first reading, the same Peter who ran to the tomb now preaches in the house of Cornelius. He tells the story of Jesus of Nazareth, "who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil," who was killed, and whom God raised on the third day. Peter can say: "We are witnesses of everything he did." The man who denied Jesus has become his witness.

Paul tells us what Easter means for us: "If then you were raised together with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is." Our life, he says, "is hidden with Christ in God." Easter is not only an event in the past. It changes the direction of our lives.

The psalm sings: "The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone." The one the world threw away is the foundation of everything. Today, let us renew our baptismal promises with conviction and share the joy of Easter with someone who needs it. The Easter season lasts fifty days; let the joy last that long too. Christ is risen. He is truly risen.
